items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Lee Collins played it too on the trumpet.

ctx.x: No, I don't think he did that. No?

Well, there is supposed to be such a record that was made. Now, I know Roy can play it because he has played it for me. Lee Collins played it too on the trumpet. Yeah, well, it would be much easier on the trumpet, but on the trombone, that is something. Roy has played that This is Pretty. And there was a record, I remember at the time that it was made, maybe it didn't even come out or something, but I remember the...
You were talking about John Lindsay when he played bass?

items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Preston Jackson and then a little drum roll player, what's his name again? Al Wynn. Since I've been sick I can't think of nobody's name. Al Wynn, they put me over there in Lincoln Garden.

ctx.x: Yeah, and where was your job?

Yeah, they was working down there and there. Where was Joe playing then? Joe was playing in Lincoln Garden. Lincoln Garden. Louis was working at the Dreamland, and joined the band at the Dreamland. I mean Lil was working there together. So I come to Chicago and I joined Joe's band. Well Joe had George Fields and he had a big band. He had the kind of band that he had now. He had a corner player playing with a man by the name of Bob Schaffner. He went later to the plantation with Dave Payton. So with the band…
So I said, when did y'all go home?
